messages:
mika (product): dropping the console mock for billing view — two variants: "compact-ledger" (tight rows + inline sparkbars + small denom chips) vs "summary-toolbar" (sparse rows + large toolbar actions). curious which feels better for org-level default. figma: https://figma.com/file/xyz987 (preview)
aurore (design): quick thoughts: org default should prioritize scanability. summary-toolbar reads better for execs. compact-ledger is great for power users in project scope. concern: inline sparkbars + token chips make the rows visually noisy at small widths.
lee (frontend): technical constraints: compact rows + inline sparklines + token breakdown = ~6 canvases per row. on large orgs that's 100-500 rows -> perf risk. we can render lightweight svgs for sparklines and lazy-render token chips on intersection. snippet:
```
const Row = memo(({row}) => {
  const inView = useInView(ref)
  return <tr>{inView ? <Sparkline data={row.history}/> : <Skeleton/>}</tr>
})
```
nina (a11y): two a11y nits: (1) tiny token chips have low contrast and no keyboard target; need 44x44 hit area or visible focus ring. (2) toolbar-only download action is ambiguous without selection context for screen readers. If toolbar is primary, announce "No rows selected" and expose "Download visible invoices".
aurore (design): good calls. alternative UX: keep compact rows but collapse token chips into a single toggle per-row that opens a small panel with clear copy and a larger download button. visually neat and keeps keyboard target.
devon (eng): implementation caveat: per-row expand panels will create a lot of on-demand fetches if we show invoice metadata. recommend caching invoice list per page and fetch details on expand. also add server-side rate limiter for downloads. event to log: `billing.invoice.download` with attrs: env, scope=org|project, invoice_id.
ravi (data): from last prototype run: users looking for invoice downloads expect per-row affordance 31% of the time; when only toolbar CTA exists they try search/filter first then contact support 12% more. small n but signals row affordance helps discoverability. happy to run AB on this.
deploy-bot: rollout_check: canary quota set to 5% for billing-ui; health checks: render latency < 200ms on initial paint.
mika (product): proposed hybrid: default org view = summary-toolbar with explicit label "Download visible invoices" + a compact per-row overflow (three dots) that contains Download and View details. project view = compact-ledger with inline expand for invoice actions. this tries to balance discoverability vs density. thoughts?
lee (frontend): hybrid seems fine. overflow per-row is cheap (1 button) and we only fetch menu items on click. for compact project view we can hydrate expands lazily. will need a migration plan for table rendering to virtualization v2.
nina (a11y): for hybrid ensure overflow menu has clear aria-labels: e.g., `aria-label="Row actions: Download invoice March 2026, $1,234"`. menu must be keyboard reachable and announce position in list ("item 4 of 12").
aurore (design): copy tweaks: replace column label "Tokens" with "Compute tokens" and add tooltip "Estimate of compute tokens used (not billing currency)". change toolbar CTA from "Download" to "Download invoices (visible)" to reduce ambiguity.
mika (product): approved those copy changes. next: A/B test plan 2 weeks. variant A: summary-toolbar default for org (current baseline). variant B: hybrid default. metrics: download CTR per user, support ticket start for missing invoice, and page CRT (core render time). ravi you own measurement; devon + lee instrument events. nina will run audit on both.
ravi (data): on it. will produce dashboards: downloads_by_variant, support_starts_by_variant, avg_render_ms_by_variant.
devon (eng): I'll add telemetry and throttle logic. also propose a server-side batch-download endpoint to support toolbar bulk downloads — reduces client churn.
aurore (design): posting updated frames in ~90m. adding focus-first visual state for overflow and expanded panel. link: https://figma.com/file/xyz987#frame3 :sparkles:
mika (product): thanks! action items: (1) design post final frames (aurore) (2) eng PR for overflow + bulk endpoint (devon) (3) data dashboard + baseline (ravi) (4) a11y checklist and review (nina). sync next Tue 9:30am. :white_check_mark:
